study_material.title: Ratio and Proportion - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind (a : b); a proportion states that two ratios are equal (a : b :: c : d). Ratios underpin partnership, mixture, age and income-expenditure problems, so fluency here pays off across the whole quant section.
learning_objectives: Combine two linked ratios into a single chain (a:b, b:c to a:b:c)
Divide a quantity in a given ratio
Use product of means = product of extremes in proportions
Find third, fourth and mean proportionals
Solve age, income-savings and coin problems with ratio variables

concepts.heading: 1. Ratio Basics
concepts.body: In a : b, a is the antecedent and b the consequent. A ratio is a pure number - no units. Multiplying or dividing both terms by the same non-zero number leaves it unchanged, which is why we can introduce a common multiplier x and write the actual values as ax and bx.

concepts.heading: 2. Combining Ratios
concepts.body: Given a:b = 2:3 and b:c = 4:5, make the b terms equal: LCM(3,4) = 12, so a:b = 8:12 and b:c = 12:15, giving a:b:c = 8:12:15. Chain as many ratios as needed this way.

concepts.heading: 3. Proportion
concepts.body: a : b :: c : d means a/b = c/d, and then ad = bc (product of extremes = product of means). Fourth proportional to a, b, c is the x with a:b = c:x. Third proportional to a, b is the x with a:b = b:x, i.e. x = b^2/a. Mean proportional between a and b is sqrt(ab).

concepts.heading: 4. Dividing in a Ratio
concepts.body: To divide T in the ratio p : q : r, the parts are T x p/(p+q+r), etc. If quantities are in ratio p:q and both are changed by the same addition, set up (px + k)/(qx + k) = new ratio and solve for x.

concepts.heading: 5. Special Ratio Forms
concepts.body: Duplicate ratio of a:b is a^2:b^2; sub-duplicate is sqrt(a):sqrt(b); triplicate is a^3:b^3; inverse is 1/a : 1/b = b : a. If 2A = 3B = 4C, then A:B:C = (1/2):(1/3):(1/4) = 6:4:3 (take reciprocals of the coefficients).

formulas: Third proportional to a, b = b^2/a
Mean proportional between a and b = sqrt(ab)
Fourth proportional to a, b, c = bc/a
Part of T in ratio p:(p+q+r) = T x p/(p+q+r)
shortcut_methods: Introduce a multiplier x immediately: values ax, bx
To merge a:b and b:c, scale both to LCM of the b values
common_mistakes: Adding ratios term-wise (2:3 plus 1:2 is NOT 3:5)
Comparing ratios of quantities in different units
Forgetting that equal additions to both terms change the ratio
study_material.summary: Write actual values with a multiplier, merge chained ratios via the common term, and use cross-multiplication for proportions. Most problems then reduce to one linear equation.
quick_revision_notes: Divide T in p:q:r by multiplying T by each share over the total

solved_examples.question: If a:b = 2:3 and b:c = 4:5, find a:b:c.
solved_examples.step_by_step: Make b equal: a:b = 8:12, b:c = 12:15. So a:b:c = 8:12:15.
solved_examples.shortcut: Multiply first ratio by 4 and second by 3 (LCM of 3 and 4 is 12).

solved_examples.question: Divide Rs. 600 among A, B, C in the ratio 2:3:5.
Find the mean proportional between 4 and 25.
The incomes of A and B are in ratio 3:4 and their expenditures in ratio 2:3. If each saves Rs. 200, find A's income.
solved_examples.step_by_step: Let incomes be 3x, 4x and expenditures 2y, 3y. Then 3x - 2y = 200 and 4x - 3y = 200. Solving: x = 200, so A's income = 600.
solved_examples.shortcut: Subtract the equations: x - y = 0, so y = x; then 3x - 2x = 200.

solved_examples.question: Two numbers are in ratio 4:5. If 8 is added to each, the ratio becomes 6:7. Find the numbers.
solved_examples.step_by_step: (4x+8)/(5x+8) = 6/7 gives 28x + 56 = 30x + 48, so x = 4. Numbers are 16 and 20.
